docs.title: State Ownership
docs.scope: The state-ownership spine (porting-rules §B made concrete): the master table mapping every Raven engine+module global to its owning Rust struct/crate/threading; the two-island model; GameWorld; the reentrancy and error-recovery contracts. NON-goals: seam executor mechanics (engine-seam.md), per-subsystem internals (docs/subsystems/*), lifecycle sequences (lifecycle.md).
decisions: STATE-D1: The two-island model. One owned per-mode Engine struct (fields = owned subsystem structs: Common{cvars,cmd,cbuf,fs,net}, Option<Server>, Option<Client>, sound, ...), created in main(), passed &mut DOWN call chains via reborrows; callers never hold borrows ACROSS nested calls (matching oracle's SV_Frame shape). Module state is a separate owned GameWorld island. Engine<->module entity aliasing goes exclusively through the raw LocateGameData-family seam (unsafe, §D11) in NativeDll AND Static transports, so the borrow checker never sees it. Module logic uses EntityId(u32) re-borrow discipline (pass (world, id), re-index per access — GP2 precedent). No RefCell, no effect queues (queues would break same-frame link-then-query parity, e.g. G_TouchTriggers observing entities linked earlier in the frame). Seam dispatchers/entrypoints use extern "C-unwind" so com_error panics traverse live C frames when hosting real DLLs (backtraces through foreign frames resolve as module+offset). The adopted diagram is docs/architecture/two-island-model.md — incorporate it as a section.

STATE-D2: GameWorld shape. Per-mode GameWorld owned by the module crate: level_locals + contiguous #[repr(C)] entity storage (boxed MAX_GENTITIES array of the already-asserted gentity_t) + MP clients array (SP has no g_clients — divergence preserved). Aliasing is preserved exactly (§A2 — no copy-narrowing; copy-based CL_GetSnapshot stays a copy because the oracle copies there). MULTI-WORLD CONSTRAINT (user requirement): GameWorld is a value type and the engine's server state holds *a* seam registration — multiple concurrent worlds with cross-world messaging must be structurally retrofittable (no singleton assumptions, no ambient statics, registration-keyed design); single-world remains the built configuration. clipMap/CollisionWorld and svEntity/worldSector state are likewise instance-shaped values.

STATE-D3: Error recovery ordering. com_error(level, msg) runs oracle's per-level recovery synchronously BEFORE panicking (mirroring SV_Shutdown -> GAME_SHUTDOWN -> free happening pre-throw at oracle/oracle/codemp/qcommon/common.cpp:313-326), then panic_any(typed payload); catch_unwind at com_frame prints and continues (DEC-08). Guards held across seam calls must be Drop-safe (no mem::forget, no manual save/restore without a guard type); Raven's skipped currentVM restore on unwind (vm.cpp:826-827) is a bug we do NOT reproduce — there is no current-module global at all.

STATE-D4: Globals collapse policy. Cleanly-bounded subsystems become owned structs under Engine (CvarSystem, CmdSystem+Cbuf incl. owned tokenizer scratch, FileSystem, NetLoopbacks, CollisionWorld, KeyState(kg), SoundSystem, ...). The zone/hunk allocator is NOT ported (rules §C9): Rust ownership replaces TheZone; hunk clear-points (map-load lifetime) become explicit owned-arena drops where behavior is observable. cmd_functions divergence preserved per-mode (SP fixed 256 array with its overflow behavior, MP heap linked list). SP cgame/ui state (cg/cgs/uiInfo) does NOT become process globals — owned structs threaded in, fixing SP's static-link regression (MP's isolation is the behavioral model). CORRECTION from B2 survey: the previously-flagged files_pc.cpp:2328 'static shadowing bug' is dead comment text, not real code — no shadowing behavior exists to model; drop that clause entirely. Also per B2: MAX_FILE_HANDLES is 64 on PC MP (16 was Xbox-only; SP is 16), and FS_ReadFile's live path uses Z_Malloc (hunk calls are commented out) — both flow into the state table.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.scope: Per-executable boot/frame/shutdown contracts for jamp, jampded, jasp: init ordering, frame anatomy, error recovery flow, event pump, timing, packaging. NON-goals: seam mechanics (engine-seam.md), module load/restart mechanics (module-loading.md), subsystem internals (docs/subsystems/*).
decisions: LIFE-D1: Loop ownership. jamp/jasp: winit (DEC-02) owns the loop — ApplicationHandler with ControlFlow::Poll, com_frame() called from about_to_wait, winit events translated into the ported 256-entry sysEvent ring (faithful queue semantics). The FPS-cap busy-spin is preserved as a spin pumping events (parity-faithful timing; WaitUntil rejected as timing-divergent). jampded: plain `loop { com_frame() }` with the Sleep(5)-equivalent entry pacing and polled console input. Renderer deferral (DEC-01) means the windowed path is designed now, first exercised later — early client slices boot headless (the _XBOX early-renderer block in SP Com_Init is dead code; PC SP inits the renderer inside CL_Init like MP).

LIFE-D2: Skeleton + packaging. com_init/com_frame/com_shutdown are ported PER-MODE into the {mp,sp} engine qcommon crates (they are Raven-derived and genuinely divergent: NET_Init location, CL_Init gating, journaling, msec clamps — no shared Lifecycle trait). Binary shells are thin new-code mains: crates/mp/app gets two [[bin]] targets (jamp, jampded) with a `dedicated` cargo feature swapping the client tier for null stubs, mirroring Raven's compile-time DEDICATED + null_* link substitution; the runtime dedicated-toggle path (common.cpp:1675-1687 behavior) stays in the client binary. sp/app is one bin.

LIFE-D3: Error payload taxonomy. com_error(level, msg) runs per-level recovery synchronously then panic_any(ComError{level, msg}) — recovery inside com_error BEFORE the panic (STATE-D3); com_frame's catch_unwind prints and continues; a catch also guards com_init (mirroring common.cpp:1439). ERR level enums are per-mode (MP's 5 levels incl. ERR_SERVERDISCONNECT/ERR_NEED_CD; SP's 4) per DEC-04. com_errorEntered and MP's 3-errors-in-100ms escalation live as owned Engine.common fields (rule B3). Panics WITHOUT our payload (genuine Rust bugs) are rethrown as fatal — never swallowed into the ERR_DROP path. Requires panic="unwind"; seam signatures are extern "C-unwind" (STATE-D1).

LIFE-D4: Small-fork bundle. (a) Journaling (MP-only: Com_InitJournaling + the Com_GetRealEvent tap) is ported WITH slice 0 — it is the cheapest determinism/replay lever for DEC-09 differential runs. (b) sys_milliseconds is backed by std::time::Instant behind the same base-relative i32 API (wrap semantics documented, internal monotonic u64). (c) NET_Shutdown: Raven declares it and never calls it — we do idiomatic Drop teardown with a 1-line divergence note. (d) jampded console input: faithful minimal polled line editor over raw stdin feeding SE_CONSOLE events into the same queue.

docs.title: Module Loading
docs.scope: How module artifacts are found, loaded, restarted, and unloaded per transport and per mode; the drop-in parity matrix (both directions); the SP three-way linkage; wasm artifact production. NON-goals: the typed call/dispatch mechanics (engine-seam.md), lifecycle ordering (lifecycle.md).
decisions: LOAD-D1: Shared mechanism, per-mode policy. native/platform (Raven-free replacement code) owns the loading MECHANISM: one libloading-based loader executing a ModuleSearchPolicy value. Each mode's app constructs its own policy: MP order = LoadLibrary-direct then basepath/fs_game then cdpath/fs_game (NO homepath — faithful; cite win_main.cpp:826 "%sx86.dll", unix "%si386.so"), SP = its narrower lookup. Naming per platform: x86.dll / i386.so / our .dylib addition for macOS (documented extension of the naming table, needed for OpenJK-style hosting).

LOAD-D2: Restart semantics. NativeDll and Static transports restart by drop+recreate (Raven's actual native path: destroy+recreate on map change — cite sv_init.cpp:484,662; cgame AND ui are destroyed+recreated on every map load via CL_FlushMemory; in-place VM_Restart only on map_restart). The Wasm transport ADDITIONALLY implements a QVM-style in-place reset fast path (reset linear memory to the initial data image + re-run module init) — user-selected; the design must pin exactly what reset restores and REQUIRE both restart paths produce identical observable module state (a parity test between them is part of the wasm host's acceptance).

LOAD-D3: Host-side wasm pointer shape. WasmPtr<T>(u32) newtype + bounds-checked accessors bound to the module Memory (checked, not power-of-2-masked — wasm memories aren't power-of-2; VM_ArgPtr vm.cpp:640-654 is the precedent, masking replaced by explicit bounds checks). Trap signatures and wire words stay identical (SEAM-D4); only the Wasm transport arm interprets pointer words as WasmPtr. Per-access re-resolution, never a cached base (memory.grow safety).

LOAD-D4: One crate per module, per-target entrypoints. crates/jampgame|cgame|ui|jagame stay single crates wired to their logic crates, compiled per --target (x86_64/i686 cdylib native, wasm32 for the sandbox). Entrypoint modules are cfg-gated (abi_transport::entrypoints::native vs ::wasm), structurally confining native-only code (libloading, OS types) to the native shim — the wasm32 CI compile gate then enforces it. No separate wasm wrapper crates.

LOAD-D5 (confirmations): The engine-side module registry has NO current-module global — per-slot state only, dispatch explicitly parameterized — so Raven's VM_Free currentVM/lastVM clobber bug (vm.cpp:624-625) is structurally unreproducible. SP is ALWAYS the fully-static shape (DEC-07): jagame via GetGameAPI is the only dynamic load; cgame's vmMain is reached via the vmachine shim as pure dispatch (retail's GetProcAddress-on-game-DLL piggyback path is not ported); UI is plain static calls. jampgame slice-0 hosting is NativeDll-first (SEAM-Q4 resolution in engine-seam.md).
